author_notes: Slot slot_170 hardens the transition-state restyle to L4 on the akella WebGL image-transition gallery. The reference promotes a normal-flow 'Transition state deck' to every demo route with a responsive tile row, the quiet demo palette, and a live source-cycle readout. The original defect (baseline) ships the deck on demo 1 only with a fixed-width row that overflows the phone; the smart-wrong solution (bad) additionally overgrows the tiles into oversized cards that cascade, overlap and bury the transition surface and turns their state text illegible dark-on-dark, and leaves the source-cycle readout stale after a click. The two leg-varying files are css/deck-row.css (row layout + tile sizing/contrast) and js/transition-deck.js (cross-page render presence + source-cycle readout wiring).
design_constraints: Preserve the Codrops demo identity: full-viewport transition imagery, thin serif frame text, bottom demo navigation, warm accent links, local transition textures, and understated debug controls.
Restyle the existing shared transition-state deck rather than replacing the gallery with a dashboard, separate settings page, static image, or non-interactive carousel.
The completed deck must make the loaded source set, frames held in the transition loop, active demo route, and source-cycle state visible with real DOM text at the top of every demo page.
Promote the deck consistently to demo routes index.html, index2.html, index6.html, and index8.html through shared code, not a one-off block on index.html.
The deck tile row must wrap to fit the viewport on phones so no state adds horizontal overflow beyond 24px tolerance.
The source-cycle control must re-render the source-cycle readout on click so the terminal readout names the source the operator stepped to.
Keep index.html, index2.html, index6.html, index8.html, and article.html available under their current static routes.

change_completion: Every demo page gains a visible shared 'Transition state deck' section instead of only scattered frame text and control widgets.
The deck includes visible text for the loaded source set, frames held in loop, active demo route, and the source-cycle state.
The deck is promoted across demo routes 1, 2, 6, and 8 through shared code, not a single label on the first page.
The source-cycle button re-renders the source-cycle readout so a click updates the terminal readout text.
design_consistency: The deck follows the gallery scale: compact, dark-translucent surface with the per-demo accent, readable over bright and dark transition imagery, subordinate to the full-viewport surface.

Deck tiles stay legibly sized within the deck surface with readable label/value contrast, rather than overgrowing into oversized cards that overlap and bury the transition surface with dark-on-dark text.
Frame links, demo navigation, article typography, and Codrops styling remain recognizable across the routes.
regression: WebGL Image Transitions, Previous Demo, Article, GitHub, Click the image, and demo 1-8 navigation remain visible in the captured demo states.
The article route still exposes setup, GLSL, transition, and references content after shared CSS changes.
Local image textures, three.js, dat.GUI, GSAP, and demo-specific scripts are not removed or replaced with remote-only placeholders.
responsive: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the first demo across viewports without horizontal overflow.
mobile_deck and tablet_deck keep the deck tile row inside the viewport with no clipped labels.
desktop_demo2, desktop_demo6, and desktop_demo8 protect cross-page deck continuity while keeping the original demo chrome intact.
desktop_article protects the non-demo article route after shared CSS changes.

metadata.design_goal: restyle and productize a shared cross-page component while preserving the interactive gallery, routes, and local assets
metadata.source_repo_kind: static WebGL image-transition gallery with eight demo routes, shared frame/demo navigation, click-to-advance transition state, dat.GUI debug controls, local texture assets, and an article route

problem_statement: The Akella WebGL Image Transitions repo is a static multi-demo transition gallery with eight demos, shared Codrops frame navigation, click-to-advance image state, dat.GUI controls on debug demos, local texture assets, and a long-form article route. A 'Transition state deck' was started to surface the live transition pipeline, but it only shipped on the first demo page, its tile row is a fixed-width strip that spills past the edge of a phone screen, its tiles have overgrown into oversized cards that cascade, overlap and bury the transition surface with state text left illegible dark-on-dark, and its source-cycle button no longer updates the source-cycle readout when clicked. Finish the restyle: promote the deck consistently to demo routes 1, 2, 6, and 8, keep the tile row inside the viewport on phones, size the tiles so they sit legibly on the quiet dark/accent surface without overlapping, and re-render the source-cycle readout so a click names the source the operator stepped to. Preserve the shader transitions, click behavior, demo routes, article route, local images, and dat.GUI controls.
required_content: Promote a visible shared 'Transition state deck' section to demo routes index.html, index2.html, index6.html, and index8.html rather than a detached page, hidden label, static image, or one-off block.
The deck should include real DOM text for the loaded source set, frames held in loop, active demo route, and a source-cycle state readout.
Keep the deck tile row wrapping inside the viewport on phones so no captured state adds horizontal overflow beyond the 24px tolerance.
Keep the deck tiles legibly sized inside the deck surface with readable label/value contrast, not overgrown cards that overlap and bury the transition surface with dark-on-dark text.
Re-render the source-cycle readout on click so the terminal readout names the stepped source (for example 'Queued source: img/img12.jpg').
Keep the click-to-advance transition behavior working on index.html and the demo 1 through demo 8 navigation, Previous Demo, Article, and GitHub links visible.
Keep article.html readable with setup, GLSL, transition, references, and credits content after shared CSS changes.
Implement the change with existing static HTML/CSS/JS files without new dependencies, remote-only images, or placeholder copy.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the first transition demo across viewports.
desktop_deck, tablet_deck, and mobile_deck protect the promoted deck's layout and palette; the mobile states must not add horizontal overflow.
desktop_demo2, desktop_demo6, and desktop_demo8 protect cross-page deck continuity on routes with different shader/control configurations.
desktop_article protects the explanatory article route and ensures shared CSS changes do not break non-demo content.
desktop_cycle_click performs a deterministic click on the source-cycle button and protects the source-cycle readout trajectory.
Completion signals should be visible rendered DOM text in demo states, not comments, console output, hidden-only labels, or unused strings.
